unmapped_findings: Fracture mode at room temperature: transgranular cleavage (TGC); SEM (Fig. 4e) shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets (Table 2, Fig. 4e).

Room-temperature tensile test: no yield stress or total elongation reported ('-' in Table 2); Fig. 3a curve 5 shows linear elastic loading then abrupt vertical load drop at ~700 MPa, i.e. brittle fracture with negligible elongation.
Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C has higher compressive yield stress (868 MPa) but lower matrix hardness (291 HB) than Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (827 MPa, 309 HB) (Table 2, b0023).
Tension-compression asymmetry: compressive yield stress exceeds tensile yield stress at room temperature and at 650/800 °C (b0040, Figs 7 and 8).

Elevated-temperature compressive yield stress decreases monotonically with increasing temperature (no yield stress anomaly); steep drop between ~600 and 800 °C, converging to 0–100 MPa at 800 °C (Fig. 5).
